evidence_frontier: Current frontier shows local widths 8,10,12 have passed 100‑epoch confirmation with aggregate Q.ANT correct counts meeting the gate against width‑16 control (w8: 444/500 vs 448/500, w10: 444/500 vs 453/500, w12: 445/500 vs 453/500).
analysis: Observations: confirmed candidates w8, w10, and w12 each met the preregistered gate against the width‑16 control on independent seed sets, with aggregate correct counts within 10 of control. The performance gap narrows as width increases, suggesting a monotonic trend but not yet saturated. Hypothesis: a wider local width (14) will continue this trend and satisfy the same gate on a fresh seed set.
hypothesis: Increasing the local width to 14 will achieve an aggregate Q.ANT correct count that is no more than 10 below the width‑16 control when evaluated on a fresh set of seeds.

proposal.title: 100‑epoch Confirmation of Local Width 14 on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does a local width of 14 maintain performance within the predefined gate relative to the width‑16 control on unseen seeds?
proposal.rationale: Widths 8, 10, and 12 have each passed the confirmation gate, indicating that intermediate compressions retain accuracy. Testing width 14 will probe whether the accuracy advantage continues to approach the control or plateaus, providing a robustness measurement for larger but still compressed architectures.

procedure: train concurrent control model with local_width 16
evaluate both models on ECG200 test set (100 samples)
aggregate Q.ANT correct counts over 500 predictions per model

proposal.success_criteria: candidate.aggregate_qant_correct >= width16_control.aggregate_qant_correct - 10 on 500 test predictions per model (i.e., candidate_correct >= control_correct - 10).
proposal.risks: Potential that width 14 does not meet the gate, indicating diminishing returns of increased width; limited seed diversity may affect generality; computational budget constrained to 100 epochs may not capture long‑term training dynamics.
